app/src/routes/index.tsx:5, app/src/routes/pokemon.$name.tsx:5 — routes import the wrapper getHomeData/getPokemonPageData, never createServerFn

containment.rationale: Nothing experimental or beta is spread across the app: swapping nitro or the server-fn layer touches one file each, and route files see only stable primitives.

evidence: app/package.json:9 — start: node .output/server/index.mjs, the documented Nitro-based Node deployment shape from TanStack Start's stable hosting docs
app/vite.config.ts:10-13 — config matches the official build-from-scratch template plus the nitro plugin the hosting guide prescribes for Node
app/src/lib/server.ts:23 — .validator() is the current stable server-fn form (replacing removed .inputValidator())

justification.rationale: The one beta reach (nitro) is what the stable framework documents for Node deployment — there is no stable alternative for this output shape — and every newer API used is the officially recommended form. Nothing is adopted for novelty.

findings.issue: The production server pipeline depends on nitro v3 beta ('still under active development' per TanStack's hosting guide; v3 is a public beta), and ^-range on a beta build invites surprise upgrades.
findings.suggestion: Keep the lockfile committed (it is) and pin the exact nitro beta version; track the nitro v3 stable release and re-verify the build/start output path when upgrading.

findings.issue: The whole app rides on TanStack Start's first stable release line (v1.169, ~1 year old), whose pre-stable history shows API removals (inputValidator→validator, nitro-v2 plugin removed).
findings.suggestion: The centralized server-fn wrapper in app/src/lib/server.ts already contains the risk; keep it that way and budget for small migrations at minor-version bumps.

findings.issue: Vite 8 (stable since 2026-03-12) ships Rolldown 1.0.0-rc internally, so build output is produced by an RC bundler.
findings.suggestion: Informational: pin vite exactly via the lockfile and watch for the Rolldown 1.0 stable announcement; no app-code change needed.

summary: This is a conservative, idiomatic TanStack Start app: zero experimental/unstable runtime APIs, all server functions isolated in one module, and a config that mirrors the official templates. The only beta reach is the nitro/vite plugin, which is precisely what the stable framework documents for Node deployment, so it's justified but worth pinning tightly. Overall risk is low-moderate, dominated by the youth of the v1 framework and its beta server toolchain rather than by any adventurous app code.
